minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard veterans, cable access and library FY26 budget presentations; only vote was adjournment.
minutes.summary: The committee, with two new members, heard FY26 budget presentations from the veterans services officer, the public access cable committee and the library director. The town manager said her budget presentation is targeted for the next Thursday and the revenue budget was just completed. A municipal building committee report was given and the meeting adjourned.

attendees.role: presenter, chair of public access cable committee

public_comment.topic: Asked whether the public can ask questions after each presentation.
Asked whether PACK videographers are town employees and get benefits under the changed SAP; concerned about losing interest income once the studio is built.
Asked who was hosting the Zoom meeting and whether others were waiting to get in.

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn, seconded, all in favor.

budget_items.what_was_said: Benefits are under budget and the line can be reduced because fewer people are on benefits. The town manager agreed and noted it can be adjusted if more people qualify.
The state reimburses the town for part of Chapter 115 expenditures; reimbursement returns to the general fund as revenue, not to the veterans line.

budget_items.topic: Public Access enterprise fund and Comcast franchise fee
budget_items.what_was_said: PACK is self-funded from the Comcast franchise fee, which is declining year by year; estimate uses a decline rate from the last calendar year.
Part of the enterprise fund was placed in an investment fund and earns interest that stays in the fund.
Anticipated franchise income, interest and total income were given; expenses leave a very small shortfall.
Capital such as a server replacement is not in the operating budget and would come directly from the enterprise fund.
Proposed split of a state fee on streaming services; amounts are unpredictable.

budget_items.topic: Library ARPA funds for teen room
budget_items.what_was_said: Select board allocated ARPA funds to library projects including the teen room renovation.

budget_items.topic: Library FY26 budget and outside funds
budget_items.what_was_said: Outside funds anticipated this year add to the municipal budget; friends of the library contribute annually.
State certification requires a minimum municipal appropriation rising about annually; FY26 requirement was cited against the recommended budget.
State aid to the library is part of the cherry sheet and offsets the operating budget rather than adding to it.
Salary request includes a clerical/SAP increase, longevity and a vacant library assistant position.

budget_items.topic: Library interim town manager recommended budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The recommendation replaced the vacant assistant position with floating hours funding.
Request to raise the programs line; recommended budget adds a smaller amount.
Replacements are requested in the IT department budget, not the library's.
Assessment decreases for FY26 despite membership fee phase-in, but expected to rise again.
The library director said a contract was signed with a percentage increase, with implications for the overall request unclear.
The town manager said the revenue budget was completed and increased slightly from local receipts.
The committee reported a range of estimated cost for renovation and addition.

decisions.decision: Veterans benefits line to be reduced for FY26 as presented, with option to adjust later.
Town manager targets next Thursday for her budget presentation to the committee.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard FY26 budget presentations from the veterans services officer, the public access cable committee and the library director.
The veterans benefits line is to be reduced for FY26 as presented, with the option to adjust it later if more people qualify.
The public access cable fund is paid by a declining cable franchise fee, and its capital needs such as a server would come from the fund itself.
The town manager said her budget presentation is targeted for the next Thursday; no votes were taken except adjournment.

why_it_matters: The veterans line is set lower because fewer people are on benefits, and the state reimburses part of that spending to the general fund, so the town's share depends on caseload.
The cable access studio is funded by a franchise fee that is falling year by year, so its operating and capital costs are a pressure on that fund, not on the tax levy as presented.
The library's FY26 request is measured against a state minimum appropriation needed for certification, so a cut below that level could put certification at risk.
watch_next: The town manager's FY26 budget presentation to the committee, targeted for the Thursday after this meeting.
